### Observed differences

- In the later window, the loop between A36 and A37 is executed less often: A37 appears in about 48 in 100 traces (previously about 60 in 100) and averages about 0.79 occurrences per trace (previously 1.14), and A36 appears in about 21 in 100 traces (previously about 31 in 100) averaging about 0.31 occurrences (previously about 0.55); these are the two largest occurrence differences in the evidence, each larger than all but about 1–2 of 200 random re-splits. [OCC031, OCC032]
- The routing around this loop moved in the same direction: from A16, the share of continuations entering the loop via A37 fell from about 36% to 29%, while the shares continuing via A17 (about 10% to 15%) and A18 (about 13% to 17%) — both of which lead mainly on to A38 — rose; from A37, the share returning to A36 fell from about 47% to 40% while the share exiting to A38 rose from about 52% to 59%; A36 still continues to A37 in nearly all cases. [DIR016, DIR017, DIR018, DIR037, DIR036]
- In the later window, the loop formed by A39 with A40, A41 and A42 before A43 is repeated more often: A39, which occurs in every trace in both windows, now repeats within about 43 in 100 traces (previously about 31 in 100) and averages about 1.69 occurrences per trace (previously 1.52), while A40, A41 and A42 each show slightly more occurrences per trace (about +0.05 to +0.09) and more traces with repeats (recurrence up about 0.04 to 0.06) at essentially unchanged participation of 61–64 in 100 traces. [OCC033, OCC034, OCC035, OCC036]
- From A40, the share of continuations returning to A39 rose from about 31% to 40%, while the share exiting to A43 fell from about 64% to 58%. [DIR040]
- Smaller participation shifts occurred elsewhere: A02 (11 to 16 in 100 traces), A17 (18 to 24), A18 (25 to 29) and A24 (45 to 52) rose, while A10 (19 to 14), A23 (56 to 51) and A33 (54 to 49) fell, and A34 and A35 each rose by about 4–5 points. [OCC002, OCC008, OCC014, OCC015, OCC020, OCC021, OCC028, OCC029, OCC030]
- Some low-frequency activities show diffuse rerouting of their rarer outgoing edges — for example from A06 the share continuing to A44 fell from about 23% to 9% while shares to A42, A20 and A39 rose, and from A04 the share to A20 fell from about 15% to 2% while A15 rose from about 9% to 20%; A44's own outgoing profile changed almost completely, but with only 7 versus 8 observed continuations this is weak. [DIR004, DIR006, DIR044]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that the frequency of two existing repeat loops changed. The A36/A37 loop, entered from A16 and left towards A38, is traversed less often in the later window: A37 now appears in about 48 in 100 traces (previously about 60) with about 0.79 occurrences per trace (previously 1.14), A36 appears in about 21 in 100 traces (previously about 31), fewer A16 continuations enter the loop (about 36% down to 29%), and A37 exits to A38 more often (about 52% up to 59%) instead of returning to A36 (about 47% down to 40%). [OCC031, OCC032, DIR016, DIR037]

The loop around A39 with A40, A41 and A42 before A43 is traversed more often: A39, present in every trace in both windows, repeats in about 43 in 100 traces (previously about 31), A40 returns to A39 in about 40% of its continuations (previously about 31%) rather than exiting to A43, and A40, A41 and A42 repeat slightly more at stable participation. [OCC033, OCC034, OCC035, OCC036, DIR040]

Supporting signs: the A36/A37 occurrence differences are the largest in the evidence and exceed virtually all of 200 random re-splits; the directional items show the entry, loop-back and exit shares moving exactly as this hypothesis requires; and every activity involved is observed in a substantial share of traces in both windows, so this is a change in how often existing paths are taken and how often they repeat, not a replacement of one path by another. [OCC031, OCC032, DIR016, DIR037, DIR040]

Limitations: each window holds only 200 traces and no screening summary is provided, so the number of qualifying items cannot be compared with a chance expectation; the evidence cannot show whether the two loop-frequency changes are connected, and for the smaller shifts it cannot rule out sampling variation between finite samples. [OCC002, OCC008, OCC020, OCC021]

Other differences: the participation changes at A02, A10, A17, A18, A23, A24, A33, A34 and A35 and the diffuse rerouting at A04, A06, A08 and A10 are not part of the main hypothesis and may partly reflect sampling variation; A44's outgoing-profile change rests on only 7 versus 8 continuations and is weak. [OCC002, OCC008, OCC014, OCC015, OCC020, OCC021, OCC028, OCC029, OCC030, DIR004, DIR006, DIR008, DIR010, DIR044]
